newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates drop to lowest level since April.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates drop to lowest level since April.

text.p: Signs of a softer economy sent mortgage rates to their lowest levels since early April, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said on Thursday.
A week earlier, mortgage applications were off a fraction, according to another industry group.
Freddie Mac said the rate on a typical 30-year fixed-rate mortgage fell to 7.86 percent in the week ended Oct. 11 vs. 8.06 percent last week. The 15-year loan fell to 7.38 percent from 7.58 percent.
A Freddie Mac economist said interest rates fell across the board after the government on Friday issued its monthly report on employment showing a weaker job market in September.
"Weakness in last Friday's employment report relieved concerns about tightness in the labour market, thereby reducing fears of inflation accelerating," said Freddie Mac Chief Economist Frank Nothaft.
Freddie Mac said its latest rates were the lowest since the week ended April 5, when 30-year loans averaged 7.78 percent, and 15-year loans averaged 7.29 percent.
Rates declines for adjustable-rate mortgages as well, falling to 5.68 percent from 5.70 percent last week.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.50 percent, the 15-year 7.01 percent, and the adjustable-rate 5.75 percent.
Freddie Mac also said lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30- and 15-year loans, and 1.4 percent on adjustable-rate loans.

Meanwhile, the Mortgage Bankers Association of America said in the week ended Oct. 4, applications to refinance mortgages rose 0.3 percent while applications to purchase mortgages slipped 0.9 percent, resulting in an average 0.7 percent weekly decline in total applications.
